  "findings": [

      "title": "Sanitize HTML even when skipping Markdown rendering",
      "body": "Returning raw here bypasses HTML sanitization entirely. PollFeed passes feed HTML into TopicEmbed.import, where Nokogiri parses it but does not remove scripts or event-handler attributes. These posts use raw_html, and their cooked content is rendered unescaped. A feed item containing an onerror handler therefore introduces stored XSS under the forum's origin. Subsequent edits to imported posts bypass the same protection. This mode should skip Markdown conversion while still sanitizing HTML on every cook."
    },

      "body": "The tag uses `end if` without a condition instead of closing the opening conditional with `end`. This produces invalid Ruby when the ERB template is compiled, so requests for an existing embedded topic fail instead of displaying the discussion. The controller specs do not render this template and therefore miss the failure."
    },
    {
      "file": "app/models/topic_embed.rb",
      "line": 48,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "security",
      "title": "Validate redirect destinations before fetching remote articles",
      "body": "TopicRetriever validates only the initial URL's hostname, while open-uri follows HTTP redirects without applying that validation again. If the configured site exposes an external redirect endpoint, a caller can supply an allowed-host URL that redirects to a private-network service. Its response can then be imported into a public topic. The Referer check does not prevent requests from clients that supply that header themselves. Validate each redirect destination, including its resolved address, before issuing the request."
    },
    {
      "file": "app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb",
      "line": 35,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Handle RSS entries that do not have an Atom content field",
      "body": "Standard RSS entries commonly provide their body in `description` or `content:encoded`, rather than `content`. SimpleRSS exposes these as separate fields, so `i.content` is nil for such entries and calling scrub raises an exception. One such entry aborts the entire poll; it also prevents TopicRetriever from reaching its HTTP fallback when feed polling is enabled. Select the available content field and handle entries with no body safely."
    },
    {
      "file": "app/models/topic_embed.rb",
      "line": 64,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Resolve relative references using URI joining",
      "body": "The slash-prefix substitution corrupts protocol-relative URLs: `//cdn.example/image.png` becomes a path on the article's host instead of a URL on cdn.example. It also leaves path-relative references such as `images/image.png` and `../other-page` untouched, so browsers resolve them against the forum URL. Imported articles consequently contain broken images and links. Resolve href and src values against the article URL with URI joining rather than manually prefixing slashes."
    },
    {
      "file": "app/models/topic_embed.rb",
      "line": 21,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "concurrency",
      "title": "Defer post-processing jobs until the outer transaction commits",
      "body": "PostCreator#create enqueues feature_topic_users and process_post before returning. Its internal transaction joins this new outer transaction, so the topic and post are still uncommitted when those jobs are submitted. A Sidekiq worker can execute them before their records are visible, and a later failure creating TopicEmbed can leave queued work for rolled-back records. Preserve atomic creation of the embed and post, but defer job submission until the outer transaction commits."
    },
    {
      "file": "lib/tasks/disqus.thor",
      "line": 148,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Preserve the original discussion timestamp during Disqus import",
      "body": "The previous PostCreator call supplied the thread's created_at timestamp, but import_remote does not accept or forward it. Imported topics and their first posts now receive the current time, while replies still retain their historical timestamps. This makes old discussions appear newly created and gives their opening posts timestamps later than their replies. Carry the source thread timestamp through the TopicEmbed import API."
    }

findings.title: Sanitize HTML even when skipping Markdown rendering
findings.body: Returning raw here bypasses HTML sanitization entirely. PollFeed passes feed HTML into TopicEmbed.import, where Nokogiri parses it but does not remove scripts or event-handler attributes. These posts use raw_html, and their cooked content is rendered unescaped. A feed item containing an onerror handler therefore introduces stored XSS under the forum's origin. Subsequent edits to imported posts bypass the same protection. This mode should skip Markdown conversion while still sanitizing HTML on every cook.

findings.title: Close the template conditional with a plain end
findings.body: The tag uses `end if` without a condition instead of closing the opening conditional with `end`. This produces invalid Ruby when the ERB template is compiled, so requests for an existing embedded topic fail instead of displaying the discussion. The controller specs do not render this template and therefore miss the failure.

findings.title: Validate redirect destinations before fetching remote articles
findings.body: TopicRetriever validates only the initial URL's hostname, while open-uri follows HTTP redirects without applying that validation again. If the configured site exposes an external redirect endpoint, a caller can supply an allowed-host URL that redirects to a private-network service. Its response can then be imported into a public topic. The Referer check does not prevent requests from clients that supply that header themselves. Validate each redirect destination, including its resolved address, before issuing the request.

findings.title: Handle RSS entries that do not have an Atom content field
findings.body: Standard RSS entries commonly provide their body in `description` or `content:encoded`, rather than `content`. SimpleRSS exposes these as separate fields, so `i.content` is nil for such entries and calling scrub raises an exception. One such entry aborts the entire poll; it also prevents TopicRetriever from reaching its HTTP fallback when feed polling is enabled. Select the available content field and handle entries with no body safely.

findings.title: Resolve relative references using URI joining
findings.body: The slash-prefix substitution corrupts protocol-relative URLs: `//cdn.example/image.png` becomes a path on the article's host instead of a URL on cdn.example. It also leaves path-relative references such as `images/image.png` and `../other-page` untouched, so browsers resolve them against the forum URL. Imported articles consequently contain broken images and links. Resolve href and src values against the article URL with URI joining rather than manually prefixing slashes.

findings.title: Defer post-processing jobs until the outer transaction commits
findings.body: PostCreator#create enqueues feature_topic_users and process_post before returning. Its internal transaction joins this new outer transaction, so the topic and post are still uncommitted when those jobs are submitted. A Sidekiq worker can execute them before their records are visible, and a later failure creating TopicEmbed can leave queued work for rolled-back records. Preserve atomic creation of the embed and post, but defer job submission until the outer transaction commits.

findings.title: Preserve the original discussion timestamp during Disqus import
findings.body: The previous PostCreator call supplied the thread's created_at timestamp, but import_remote does not accept or forward it. Imported topics and their first posts now receive the current time, while replies still retain their historical timestamps. This makes old discussions appear newly created and gives their opening posts timestamps later than their replies. Carry the source thread timestamp through the TopicEmbed import API.
